name: Cal AI
h1: Cal AI ARR: ~$50M for Calorie Tracking by Camera, Then an Exit.
intro: Cal AI made nutrition tracking a camera action — snap the meal, get calories and macros — and rode influencer marketing to millions of downloads and an estimated ~$50M run rate, all built by founders still in their teens. In March 2026 MyFitnessPal acquired the app. The reported numbers, with sources, are below.

milestones.note: Founded by Zach Yadegari and Henry Lang Mackenzie — both teenagers — on a simple premise: tracking food by photographing it instead of typing it.
Influencer marketing on TikTok and Instagram drives millions of downloads; a low-friction annual subscription converts them.
Reaches $50M annualized run rate roughly twenty-two months after launch, per Leonis Capital's tracking.

milestones.label: Mar '26
milestones.note: MyFitnessPal acquires Cal AI, folding the camera-first tracker into the largest nutrition platform — a two-and-a-half-year run from founding to exit.

modelTitle: One Photo Instead of a Food Diary, Priced Like an App.
modelParagraphs: Every calorie app before Cal AI died on the same friction: logging meals by hand feels like homework. Cal AI replaced the diary with the camera — photograph the plate, the model estimates calories and macros — which removed the single biggest churn driver in nutrition tracking. The product insight is deletion, not addition.

Distribution was influencer marketing at relentless volume, with a cheap annual subscription converting downloads. That combination — one-step core action, creator-driven acquisition, annual prepay — is why a team of teenagers could out-earn venture-backed health apps, and why MyFitnessPal bought it in March 2026.
revenueMix: Low-friction yearly plans converting influencer-driven downloads.
Performance-priced creator marketing as the primary growth spend.

faqs.a: Around $50 million at the time of its March 2026 acquisition, estimated. Cal AI never disclosed exact revenue; the figure comes from GetLatka with Leonis Capital charting about twenty-two months from launch to $50M.
MyFitnessPal acquired the app in March 2026, per TechCrunch — bringing the camera-first tracker and its young user base into the largest established nutrition platform.
Zach Yadegari and Henry Lang Mackenzie founded it in 2023, both teenagers at the time. The company became the standard citation for young founders building revenue-first AI apps.

Photo estimation gives a close range, not a lab measurement — portion sizes are inferred from the image. Users accepted that trade because consistency matters more than precision in habit tracking, which is the job Cal AI actually does.

faqs.q: How Did Cal AI Grow Without Big Ad Budgets?
faqs.a: Influencer marketing priced per download: creators demoed the camera flow on TikTok and Instagram, the app converted viewers on an annual plan, and revenue funded the next wave of placements.
